import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reinhardt cardinals

A *Reinhardt cardinal* is the critical point of a nontrivial elementary embedding $j : V \to V$
of the set-theoretic universe into itself. Kunen (1971) showed that no such embedding exists
in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ (or in $\mathsf{NBG}$ with the axiom of choice). Suzuki (1999) showed that in
$\mathsf{ZF}$ no such embedding is definable from parameters. Whether such an embedding can
exist without the axiom of choice is open.

Following the Wikipedia article, the question is made precise as the consistency of the
first-order theory $\mathsf{ZF}_j + $ “$j$ is a nontrivial elementary embedding”: the language of
set theory is extended by a unary function symbol $j$, and the axioms are
* the axioms of $\mathsf{ZF}$, with the Separation and Collection schemas for all formulas of the
  extended language (so classes defined using $j$ are allowed),
* the elementarity scheme $\forall \vec x\,(\varphi(\vec x) \leftrightarrow \varphi(j(\vec x)))$
  for every formula $\varphi$ of the language of set theory (not mentioning $j$),
* nontriviality: $\exists x\, j(x) \neq x$.

By the completeness theorem, this theory is consistent if and only if it has a model, so the
question is stated as the satisfiability of the theory.

The file builds the language `{∈, j}` and the theory explicitly, using Mathlib's first-order
logic (`FirstOrder.Language`). The `API` lemmas at the end unfold each axiom in an arbitrary
structure, to check the variable indices.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Reinhardt cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinhardt_cardinal)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* K. Kunen, *Elementary embeddings and infinitary combinatorics*,
  J. Symbolic Logic 36 (1971), 407–413.
* A. Suzuki, *No elementary embedding from V into V is definable from parameters*,
  J. Symbolic Logic 64 (1999), 1591–1594.
-/

/-- Infinity:
`∃ x (∃ e (e ∈ x ∧ ∀ z ¬ (z ∈ e)) ∧ ∀ y (y ∈ x → ∃ s (s ∈ x ∧ ∀ z (z ∈ s ↔ z ∈ y ∨ z = y))))`,

def separation {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) : jLang.Sentence :=
  univClosure <| ∀' ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &1) ⇔ ((&2 ∈' &0) ⊓ φ.liftAt 1 1))
blocks.docstring:
The Separation axiom for a formula `φ(w⃗, z, x)` of the language `{∈, j}`, with parameters
`w⃗ : Fin k` (the free variables of `φ`) and two bound variables `z = &0`, `x = &1`:
`∀ w⃗ ∀ z ∃ y ∀ x (x ∈ y ↔ (x ∈ z ∧ φ(w⃗, z, x)))`.
The new variable `y` (`&1` in the axiom) is not free in `φ`; `φ.liftAt 1 1` shifts `x` to `&2`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `ZFSet` (Lean's internal model of ZFC) — unusable, since the question is about consistency of a theory and Lean's metatheory has choice, so Kunen's theorem would make any `j : ZFSet → ZFSet` version trivially false.

/-- The Separation axiom for a formula `φ(w⃗, z, x)` of the language `{∈, j}`, with parameters
`w⃗ : Fin k` (the free variables of `φ`) and two bound variables `z = &0`, `x = &1`:
`∀ w⃗ ∀ z ∃ y ∀ x (x ∈ y ↔ (x ∈ z ∧ φ(w⃗, z, x)))`.
The new variable `y` (`&1` in the axiom) is not free in `φ`; `φ.liftAt 1 1` shifts `x` to `&2`. -/
def separation {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) : jLang.Sentence :=
  univClosure <| ∀' ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &1) ⇔ ((&2 ∈' &0) ⊓ φ.liftAt 1 1))

blocks.docstring:
The Collection axiom for a formula `φ(w⃗, x, y)` of the language `{∈, j}`, with parameters
`w⃗ : Fin k` (the free variables of `φ`) and two bound variables `x = &0`, `y = &1`:
`∀ w⃗ ∀ a (∀ x (x ∈ a → ∃ y φ(w⃗, x, y)) → ∃ b ∀ x (x ∈ a → ∃ y (y ∈ b ∧ φ(w⃗, x, y))))`.
The new variables `a` and `b` are not free in `φ`; `φ.liftAt 1 0` and `φ.liftAt 2 0` shift `x, y`
to `&1, &2` and to `&2, &3` respectively.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `ZFSet` (Lean's internal model of ZFC) — unusable, since the question is about consistency of a theory and Lean's metatheory has choice, so Kunen's theorem would make any `j : ZFSet → ZFSet` version trivially false.

blocks.name: collection
blocks.text:
/-- The Collection axiom for a formula `φ(w⃗, x, y)` of the language `{∈, j}`, with parameters
`w⃗ : Fin k` (the free variables of `φ`) and two bound variables `x = &0`, `y = &1`:
`∀ w⃗ ∀ a (∀ x (x ∈ a → ∃ y φ(w⃗, x, y)) → ∃ b ∀ x (x ∈ a → ∃ y (y ∈ b ∧ φ(w⃗, x, y))))`.
The new variables `a` and `b` are not free in `φ`; `φ.liftAt 1 0` and `φ.liftAt 2 0` shift `x, y`
to `&1, &2` and to `&2, &3` respectively. -/
def collection {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) : jLang.Sentence :=
  univClosure <| ∀' ((∀' ((&1 ∈' &0) ⟹ ∃' φ.liftAt 1 0)) ⟹
    ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &0) ⟹ ∃' ((&3 ∈' &1) ⊓ φ.liftAt 2 0)))

Collection schemas range over all formulas of the extended language (including those
mentioning `j`).

blocks.name: zfJ
blocks.text:
/-- The theory `ZF_j`: the axioms of `ZF` in the language `{∈, j}`, where the Separation and
Collection schemas range over all formulas of the extended language (including those
mentioning `j`). -/
def zfJ : jLang.Theory :=
  {extensionality, emptySet, pairing, union, powerset, infinity, foundation} ∪
    {σ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2), σ = separation φ} ∪
    {σ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2), σ = collection φ}

blocks.text:
/-- The elementarity axiom for a formula `φ(x₀, …, x_{k-1})` of the language of set theory `{∈}`
(not mentioning `j`): `∀ x⃗ (φ(x⃗) ↔ φ(j(x₀), …, j(x_{k-1})))`. -/

  univClosure <| (setLangHom.onFormula φ) ⇔
    (setLangHom.onFormula φ).subst fun i => japp (Term.var i)

def reinhardtTheory : jLang.Theory :=
  zfJ ∪ {σ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : setLang.Formula (Fin k)), σ = elementarity φ} ∪ {nontrivial}

together with a Reinhardt embedding; its critical point is a Reinhardt cardinal.

  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Reinhardt cardinals.** Without assuming the axiom of choice, can a nontrivial elementary
embedding $j : V \to V$ exist? That is, is the theory
$\mathsf{ZF}_j + $ “$j : V \to V$ is a nontrivial elementary embedding” consistent, where
$\mathsf{ZF}_j$ is $\mathsf{ZF}$ in the language with the extra function symbol $j$, with
Separation and Collection for all formulas involving $j$?

By the completeness theorem, consistency of the theory is equivalent to the existence of a
model, so the question is formalized as `reinhardtTheory.IsSatisfiable`. A positive answer
(`answer(True)`) means that such an embedding can consistently exist; a negative answer means
that Reinhardt cardinals are inconsistent with `ZF`.

Here `j` is a primitive function symbol, not a class definable from parameters: Suzuki (1999)
showed that no definable class is such an embedding. The axiom of choice is not assumed: Kunen
(1971) showed that no such embedding exists in `ZFC` (or `NBG` with choice).

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem exists_elementaryEmbedding [M ⊨ reinhardtTheory] :
    letI := setLangHom.reduct M
    ∃ e : M ↪ₑ[setLang] M, (∀ x, e x = jₘ x) ∧ ∃ x, e x ≠ x := by
  letI := setLangHom.reduct M
  have hj : ∀ ⦃k : ℕ⦄ (φ : setLang.Formula (Fin k)) (v : Fin k → M),
      φ.Realize ((fun x => jₘ x) ∘ v) ↔ φ.Realize v := by
    intro k φ v
    have hmem : elementarity φ ∈ reinhardtTheory :=
      Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_union_right _ ⟨k, φ, rfl⟩)
    exact ((realize_elementarity φ).1 (Theory.Model.realize_of_mem (M := M) _ hmem) v).symm
  have hn : M ⊨ nontrivial :=
    Theory.Model.realize_of_mem (M := M) (T := reinhardtTheory) _ (Set.mem_union_right _ rfl)
  exact ⟨⟨fun x => jₘ x, hj⟩, fun _ => rfl, realize_nontrivial.1 hn⟩

claims.decomposer_note: A single yes/no consistency question: is the theory ZF (with an added function symbol j and Separation/Collection for all formulas involving j — equivalently a class theory such as NBG without choice) plus 'j is a nontrivial elementary embedding V→V' consistent? The formalization must not read j as a ZF-definable class (Suzuki 1999 refutes that), and must omit AC (Kunen 1971 refutes the ZFC/NBG+AC version); the Prop is the consistency/satisfiability of an explicitly built first-order theory, and the article's stronger axioms (super Reinhardt, J1–J3, Berkeley) and the V_{λ+2}/V_{λ+3} results are context, not further questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c02 builds the first-order theory ZF_j + 'j is a nontrivial elementary embedding' explicitly in Mathlib's FirstOrder.Language: language {∈, j} with j a primitive unary function symbol (not a definable class); Extensionality, Empty set, Pairing, Union, Power set, Infinity, Foundation; Separation and Collection schemas over ALL {∈, j}-formulas (parameters as Fin k free variables, closed by univClosure); elementarity scheme ∀x⃗ (φ(x⃗) ↔ φ(j x⃗)) over all {∈}-formulas transported via the language inclusion; ∃x, j x ≠ x; no choice axiom. The Prop is `answer(sorry) ↔ reinhardtTheory.IsSatisfiable`, with answer(True) = the embedding can consistently exist. Crucially, every axiom (including the de Bruijn-indexed schemas) is pinned down by a fully proved `realize_*` lemma unfolding it to the textbook statement in an arbitrary structure, so the encoding is verified rather than trusted. import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reinhardt cardinals

A *Reinhardt cardinal* is the critical point of a nontrivial elementary embedding $j : V \to V$
of the set-theoretic universe into itself. Kunen (1971) showed that no such embedding exists
in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ (or in $\mathsf{NBG}$ with the axiom of choice). Suzuki (1999) showed that in
$\mathsf{ZF}$ no such embedding is definable from parameters. Whether such an embedding can
exist without the axiom of choice is open.

Following the Wikipedia article, the question is made precise as the consistency of the
first-order theory $\mathsf{ZF}_j + $ “$j$ is a nontrivial elementary embedding”: the language of
set theory is extended by a unary function symbol $j$, and the axioms are
* the axioms of $\mathsf{ZF}$, with the Separation and Collection schemas for all formulas of the
  extended language (so classes defined using $j$ are allowed),
* the elementarity scheme $\forall \vec x\,(\varphi(\vec x) \leftrightarrow \varphi(j(\vec x)))$
  for every formula $\varphi$ of the language of set theory (not mentioning $j$),
* nontriviality: $\exists x\, j(x) \neq x$.

By the completeness theorem, this theory is consistent if and only if it has a model, so the
question is stated as the satisfiability of the theory.

The file builds the language `{∈, j}` and the theory explicitly, using Mathlib's first-order
logic (`FirstOrder.Language`). The `API` lemmas at the end unfold each axiom in an arbitrary
structure, to check the variable indices.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Reinhardt cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinhardt_cardinal)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* K. Kunen, *Elementary embeddings and infinitary combinatorics*,
  J. Symbolic Logic 36 (1971), 407–413.
* A. Suzuki, *No elementary embedding from V into V is definable from parameters*,
  J. Symbolic Logic 64 (1999), 1591–1594.
-/

namespace ReinhardtCardinals

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- The relation symbols of the language of set theory: one binary relation `∈`. -/
inductive SetRel : ℕ → Type
  | mem : SetRel 2

/-- The function symbols added to the language of set theory: one unary function `j`. -/
inductive JFunc : ℕ → Type
  | j : JFunc 1

/-- The language of set theory `{∈}`. -/
def setLang : Language := ⟨fun _ => Empty, SetRel⟩

/-- The language of set theory with one extra unary function symbol: `{∈, j}`. -/
def jLang : Language := ⟨JFunc, SetRel⟩

/-- The inclusion of the language `{∈}` into the language `{∈, j}`. -/
def setLangHom : setLang →ᴸ jLang := ⟨fun _ => Empty.elim, fun _ => id⟩

/-- The atomic formula `t₁ ∈ t₂` of the language `{∈, j}`. -/
def memRel {α : Type} {n : ℕ} (t₁ t₂ : jLang.Term (α ⊕ Fin n)) : jLang.BoundedFormula α n :=
  Relations.boundedFormula₂ SetRel.mem t₁ t₂

@[inherit_doc] local infixl:88 " ∈' " => memRel

/-- The term `j(t)` of the language `{∈, j}`. -/
def japp {α : Type} (t : jLang.Term α) : jLang.Term α :=
  Functions.apply₁ JFunc.j t

/-- The universal closure `∀ x₀ … ∀ x_{k-1}, φ` of a formula `φ` with free variables in `Fin k`. -/
def univClosure {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.Formula (Fin k)) : jLang.Sentence :=
  (BoundedFormula.relabel (Sum.inr : Fin k → Empty ⊕ Fin k) φ).alls

/-
### The axioms of `ZF` in the language `{∈, j}`

Bound variables are written with de Bruijn indices: `&0` is the outermost quantified variable.
-/

/-- Extensionality: `∀ x ∀ y (∀ z (z ∈ x ↔ z ∈ y) → x = y)`. -/
def extensionality : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∀' ∀' ((∀' ((&2 ∈' &0) ⇔ (&2 ∈' &1))) ⟹ (&0 =' &1))

/-- Empty set: `∃ x ∀ y ¬ (y ∈ x)`. -/
def emptySet : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∃' ∀' ∼(&1 ∈' &0)

/-- Pairing: `∀ x ∀ y ∃ p ∀ z (z ∈ p ↔ z = x ∨ z = y)`. -/
def pairing : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∀' ∀' ∃' ∀' ((&3 ∈' &2) ⇔ ((&3 =' &0) ⊔ (&3 =' &1)))

/-- Union: `∀ x ∃ u ∀ z (z ∈ u ↔ ∃ y (y ∈ x ∧ z ∈ y))`. -/
def union : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∀' ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &1) ⇔ ∃' ((&3 ∈' &0) ⊓ (&2 ∈' &3)))

/-- Power set: `∀ x ∃ p ∀ z (z ∈ p ↔ ∀ w (w ∈ z → w ∈ x))`. -/
def powerset : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∀' ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &1) ⇔ ∀' ((&3 ∈' &2) ⟹ (&3 ∈' &0)))

/-- Infinity:
`∃ x (∃ e (e ∈ x ∧ ∀ z ¬ (z ∈ e)) ∧ ∀ y (y ∈ x → ∃ s (s ∈ x ∧ ∀ z (z ∈ s ↔ z ∈ y ∨ z = y))))`,
i.e. there is a set containing the empty set and closed under `y ↦ y ∪ {y}`. -/
def infinity : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∃' ((∃' ((&1 ∈' &0) ⊓ ∀' ∼(&2 ∈' &1))) ⊓
    ∀' ((&1 ∈' &0) ⟹ ∃' ((&2 ∈' &0) ⊓ ∀' ((&3 ∈' &2) ⇔ ((&3 ∈' &1) ⊔ (&3 =' &1))))))

/-- Foundation (regularity): `∀ x (∃ y (y ∈ x) → ∃ y (y ∈ x ∧ ∀ z (z ∈ y → ¬ (z ∈ x))))`. -/
def foundation : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∀' ((∃' (&1 ∈' &0)) ⟹ ∃' ((&1 ∈' &0) ⊓ ∀' ((&2 ∈' &1) ⟹ ∼(&2 ∈' &0))))

/-- The Separation axiom for a formula `φ(w⃗, z, x)` of the language `{∈, j}`, with parameters
`w⃗ : Fin k` (the free variables of `φ`) and two bound variables `z = &0`, `x = &1`:
`∀ w⃗ ∀ z ∃ y ∀ x (x ∈ y ↔ (x ∈ z ∧ φ(w⃗, z, x)))`.
The new variable `y` (`&1` in the axiom) is not free in `φ`; `φ.liftAt 1 1` shifts `x` to `&2`. -/
def separation {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) : jLang.Sentence :=
  univClosure <| ∀' ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &1) ⇔ ((&2 ∈' &0) ⊓ φ.liftAt 1 1))

/-- The Collection axiom for a formula `φ(w⃗, x, y)` of the language `{∈, j}`, with parameters
`w⃗ : Fin k` (the free variables of `φ`) and two bound variables `x = &0`, `y = &1`:
`∀ w⃗ ∀ a (∀ x (x ∈ a → ∃ y φ(w⃗, x, y)) → ∃ b ∀ x (x ∈ a → ∃ y (y ∈ b ∧ φ(w⃗, x, y))))`.
The new variables `a` and `b` are not free in `φ`; `φ.liftAt 1 0` and `φ.liftAt 2 0` shift `x, y`
to `&1, &2` and to `&2, &3` respectively. -/
def collection {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) : jLang.Sentence :=
  univClosure <| ∀' ((∀' ((&1 ∈' &0) ⟹ ∃' φ.liftAt 1 0)) ⟹
    ∃' ∀' ((&2 ∈' &0) ⟹ ∃' ((&3 ∈' &1) ⊓ φ.liftAt 2 0)))

/-- The theory `ZF_j`: the axioms of `ZF` in the language `{∈, j}`, where the Separation and
Collection schemas range over all formulas of the extended language (including those
mentioning `j`). -/
def zfJ : jLang.Theory :=
  {extensionality, emptySet, pairing, union, powerset, infinity, foundation} ∪
    {σ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2), σ = separation φ} ∪
    {σ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2), σ = collection φ}

/-
### `j` is a nontrivial elementary embedding `V → V`
-/

/-- The elementarity axiom for a formula `φ(x₀, …, x_{k-1})` of the language of set theory `{∈}`
(not mentioning `j`): `∀ x⃗ (φ(x⃗) ↔ φ(j(x₀), …, j(x_{k-1})))`. -/
def elementarity {k : ℕ} (φ : setLang.Formula (Fin k)) : jLang.Sentence :=
  univClosure <| (setLangHom.onFormula φ) ⇔
    (setLangHom.onFormula φ).subst fun i => japp (Term.var i)

/-- Nontriviality: `∃ x, j(x) ≠ x`. -/
def nontrivial : jLang.Sentence :=
  ∃' ∼(japp (&0) =' &0)

/-- The theory `ZF_j + "j : V → V is a nontrivial elementary embedding"`: `ZF` with Separation and
Collection for all formulas involving `j`, the elementarity scheme for all formulas of the
language of set theory, and `∃ x, j(x) ≠ x`. A model of this theory is a universe of `ZF`
together with a Reinhardt embedding; its critical point is a Reinhardt cardinal. -/
def reinhardtTheory : jLang.Theory :=
  zfJ ∪ {σ | ∃ (k : ℕ) (φ : setLang.Formula (Fin k)), σ = elementarity φ} ∪ {nontrivial}

/--
**Reinhardt cardinals.** Without assuming the axiom of choice, can a nontrivial elementary
embedding $j : V \to V$ exist? That is, is the theory
$\mathsf{ZF}_j + $ “$j : V \to V$ is a nontrivial elementary embedding” consistent, where
$\mathsf{ZF}_j$ is $\mathsf{ZF}$ in the language with the extra function symbol $j$, with
Separation and Collection for all formulas involving $j$?

By the completeness theorem, consistency of the theory is equivalent to the existence of a
model, so the question is formalized as `reinhardtTheory.IsSatisfiable`. A positive answer
(`answer(True)`) means that such an embedding can consistently exist; a negative answer means
that Reinhardt cardinals are inconsistent with `ZF`.

Here `j` is a primitive function symbol, not a class definable from parameters: Suzuki (1999)
showed that no definable class is such an embedding. The axiom of choice is not assumed: Kunen
(1971) showed that no such embedding exists in `ZFC` (or `NBG` with choice).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem reinhardt_cardinals : answer(sorry) ↔ reinhardtTheory.IsSatisfiable := by
  sorry

/-
### API: the meaning of the axioms in a structure

Each lemma unfolds one axiom in an arbitrary `{∈, j}`-structure `M`.
-/

section API

variable {M : Type} [jLang.Structure M]

/-- The interpretation of `∈` in `M`. -/
local notation:50 x " ∈ₘ " y => Structure.RelMap (L := jLang) SetRel.mem ![x, y]

/-- The interpretation of `j` in `M`. -/
local notation "jₘ" => fun x => Structure.funMap (L := jLang) JFunc.j ![x]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_memRel {α : Type} {n : ℕ} {t₁ t₂ : jLang.Term (α ⊕ Fin n)} {v : α → M}
    {xs : Fin n → M} :
    (t₁ ∈' t₂).Realize v xs ↔ (t₁.realize (Sum.elim v xs) ∈ₘ t₂.realize (Sum.elim v xs)) := by
  simp [memRel, BoundedFormula.realize_rel₂]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_japp {α : Type} {t : jLang.Term α} {v : α → M} :
    (japp t).realize v = jₘ (t.realize v) := by
  simp [japp]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_univClosure {k : ℕ} {φ : jLang.Formula (Fin k)} :
    M ⊨ univClosure φ ↔ ∀ v : Fin k → M, φ.Realize v := by
  rw [univClosure, Sentence.Realize, BoundedFormula.realize_alls]
  refine forall_congr' fun xs => ?_
  rw [Formula.Realize, BoundedFormula.realize_relabel, Sum.elim_comp_inr, Fin.castAdd_zero,
    Fin.cast_refl, Function.comp_id, Subsingleton.elim (xs ∘ Fin.natAdd k) default]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_extensionality :
    M ⊨ extensionality ↔ ∀ x y : M, (∀ z, (z ∈ₘ x) ↔ (z ∈ₘ y)) → x = y := by
  simp [extensionality, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_emptySet :
    M ⊨ emptySet ↔ ∃ x : M, ∀ y, ¬ (y ∈ₘ x) := by
  simp [emptySet, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_pairing :
    M ⊨ pairing ↔ ∀ x y : M, ∃ p, ∀ z, (z ∈ₘ p) ↔ z = x ∨ z = y := by
  simp [pairing, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_union :
    M ⊨ union ↔ ∀ x : M, ∃ u, ∀ z, (z ∈ₘ u) ↔ ∃ y, (y ∈ₘ x) ∧ (z ∈ₘ y) := by
  simp [union, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_powerset :
    M ⊨ powerset ↔ ∀ x : M, ∃ p, ∀ z, (z ∈ₘ p) ↔ ∀ w, (w ∈ₘ z) → (w ∈ₘ x) := by
  simp [powerset, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_infinity :
    M ⊨ infinity ↔ ∃ x : M, (∃ e, (e ∈ₘ x) ∧ ∀ z, ¬ (z ∈ₘ e)) ∧
      ∀ y, (y ∈ₘ x) → ∃ s, (s ∈ₘ x) ∧ ∀ z, (z ∈ₘ s) ↔ (z ∈ₘ y) ∨ z = y := by
  simp [infinity, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_foundation :
    M ⊨ foundation ↔ ∀ x : M, (∃ y, y ∈ₘ x) → ∃ y, (y ∈ₘ x) ∧ ∀ z, (z ∈ₘ y) → ¬ (z ∈ₘ x) := by
  simp [foundation, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_separation {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) :
    M ⊨ separation φ ↔ ∀ (w : Fin k → M) (z : M), ∃ y, ∀ x,
      (x ∈ₘ y) ↔ (x ∈ₘ z) ∧ φ.Realize w ![z, x] := by
  simp [separation, realize_univClosure, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc,
    BoundedFormula.realize_liftAt_one (show 1 ≤ 2 by norm_num)]
  refine forall_congr' fun w => forall_congr' fun z => exists_congr fun y =>
    forall_congr' fun x => ?_
  congr! 3
  funext i
  fin_cases i <;> rfl

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_collection {k : ℕ} (φ : jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2) :
    M ⊨ collection φ ↔ ∀ (w : Fin k → M) (a : M),
      (∀ x, (x ∈ₘ a) → ∃ y, φ.Realize w ![x, y]) →
        ∃ b, ∀ x, (x ∈ₘ a) → ∃ y, (y ∈ₘ b) ∧ φ.Realize w ![x, y] := by
  simp [collection, realize_univClosure, Formula.Realize, realize_memRel, Fin.snoc,
    BoundedFormula.realize_liftAt_one (show 0 ≤ 2 by norm_num),
    BoundedFormula.realize_liftAt (show 0 + 2 ≤ 2 + 1 by norm_num)]
  refine forall_congr' fun w => forall_congr' fun a => imp_congr ?_ ?_
  · refine forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr_right fun _ => exists_congr fun y => ?_
    congr! 2
    funext i
    fin_cases i <;> rfl
  · refine exists_congr fun b => forall_congr' fun x => imp_congr_right fun _ =>
      exists_congr fun y => and_congr_right fun _ => ?_
    congr! 2
    funext i
    fin_cases i <;> rfl

/-- `M ⊨ elementarity φ` says that `j` preserves `φ`, where `φ` is interpreted in the
`{∈}`-reduct of `M`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_elementarity {k : ℕ} (φ : setLang.Formula (Fin k)) :
    M ⊨ elementarity φ ↔ ∀ v : Fin k → M,
      (letI := setLangHom.reduct M; φ.Realize v ↔ φ.Realize (jₘ ∘ v)) := by
  letI := setLangHom.reduct M
  refine realize_univClosure.trans (forall_congr' fun v => ?_)
  rw [Formula.realize_iff, LHom.realize_onFormula, Formula.Realize, Formula.Realize,
    BoundedFormula.realize_subst]
  exact iff_congr Iff.rfl <| (LHom.realize_onFormula setLangHom φ).trans <| by
    simp [realize_japp, Function.comp_def]

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem realize_nontrivial :
    M ⊨ nontrivial ↔ ∃ x : M, jₘ x ≠ x := by
  simp [nontrivial, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, realize_japp, Fin.snoc]

/-- In a model `M` of `reinhardtTheory`, the interpretation of `j` is an elementary embedding of
the `{∈}`-reduct of `M` into itself (in the sense of `FirstOrder.Language.ElementaryEmbedding`)
that is not the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem exists_elementaryEmbedding [M ⊨ reinhardtTheory] :
    letI := setLangHom.reduct M
    ∃ e : M ↪ₑ[setLang] M, (∀ x, e x = jₘ x) ∧ ∃ x, e x ≠ x := by
  letI := setLangHom.reduct M
  have hj : ∀ ⦃k : ℕ⦄ (φ : setLang.Formula (Fin k)) (v : Fin k → M),
      φ.Realize ((fun x => jₘ x) ∘ v) ↔ φ.Realize v := by
    intro k φ v
    have hmem : elementarity φ ∈ reinhardtTheory :=
      Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_union_right _ ⟨k, φ, rfl⟩)
    exact ((realize_elementarity φ).1 (Theory.Model.realize_of_mem (M := M) _ hmem) v).symm
  have hn : M ⊨ nontrivial :=
    Theory.Model.realize_of_mem (M := M) (T := reinhardtTheory) _ (Set.mem_union_right _ rfl)
  exact ⟨⟨fun x => jₘ x, hj⟩, fun _ => rfl, realize_nontrivial.1 hn⟩

end API

end ReinhardtCardinals

items: Consistency of the theory is formalized as Mathlib's `Theory.IsSatisfiable` (existence of a nonempty model in `Type`); these agree by the Gödel completeness theorem (and Löwenheim–Skolem, since the language is countable), so `answer(True)` means the theory is consistent.

Following the Wikipedia article's first option (rather than NBG/KM), the theory is ZF in the language with an extra unary function symbol j, with the Separation and Collection schemas ranging over all formulas of the extended language (formulas mentioning j included). Collection is used (as the article says) rather than Replacement; over the other axioms with Separation these are equivalent.

ZF axioms included: Extensionality, Empty set (redundant but harmless), Pairing, Union, Power set, Infinity, Foundation as a single axiom (the ∈-induction scheme for j-formulas follows from it plus Separation_j in ZF_j), Separation and Collection schemas.

Schema instances are parameterized by formulas `jLang.BoundedFormula (Fin k) 2` for every `k : ℕ` (parameters w⃗ as free variables, the two designated variables as bound variables), so all finite parameter counts are covered; fresh variables are inserted with `BoundedFormula.liftAt`, so they are never free in φ.

'j is an elementary embedding V → V' is the scheme ∀x⃗ (φ(x⃗) ↔ φ(j(x⃗))) for all formulas φ of the pure language {∈} (not mentioning j), transported into {∈, j} via the language inclusion `setLangHom`; this is the standard notion (elementarity with respect to (V, ∈)). Injectivity and ∈-preservation are instances.
'Nontrivial' is ∃x, j(x) ≠ x. The critical point (the Reinhardt cardinal itself) is not mentioned since the statement only asks about existence of the embedding.
Universal closures are computed with `BoundedFormula.relabel Sum.inr` followed by `alls`, avoiding the choice-dependent `Formula.iAlls`.

The stronger axioms (super Reinhardt, J1–J3, Berkeley) and the V_{λ+2}/V_{λ+3} results in the article are treated as context, per the decomposition table; only the single consistency question is stated.

Rejected as unfaithful. c08 uses the correct convention but its 'pairing' axiom is actually binary union (z∈p ↔ z∈x ∨ z∈y); the resulting theory is still equivalent to ZF_j (pairing is derivable from Collection+Separation+Power set), but the file is mislabeled, and its Separation/Collection encodings are unverified — not chosen. c07 is faithful but encodes the theory as the set of sentences valid on a semantic model class (convoluted). Modeling notes for a human: (1) consistency is rendered as Mathlib `Theory.IsSatisfiable` (model in Type 0); equivalence with syntactic consistency is by completeness + downward Löwenheim–Skolem for this countable language, in Lean's classical metatheory. (2) Following the Wikipedia article, the ZF-with-function-symbol formulation was chosen over the NBG/KM class-theory formulation; the decomposition note allows either. (4) Foundation is the single regularity axiom; with Separation for j-formulas this yields ∈-induction for j-formulas. (5) The cited arXiv preprint claiming inconsistency (McCallum 2026) was withdrawn per the article, so the problem remains open and is tagged `research open`.
